fact: Private member's bill no 53, tabled in the Chamber of Councillors on 17 April 2024 by the UGTM group, aims to prevent malicious uses of content generation such as deepfakes and would create a National Artificial Intelligence Agency.

fact: The Mouvement populaire group in the House of Representatives tabled a private member's bill regulating AI use that bars AI on social media from spreading false news, abusive speech or fabricated images and videos, bans unacceptable-risk systems from the market, and sets fines of MAD 50,000-500,000 and prison of 6 months to 5 years.
system: Proposed law on regulating the use of artificial intelligence

fact: Analyst Meryem Aanaiber writes in Telquel that Penal Code Articles 447-1 to 447-3 (added by Law No. 103-13 of 2018) are the most directly applicable legal basis against deepfakes, with penalties of one to three years' imprisonment for 447-2, though no law defines deepfakes.
Telquel's op-ed says a 17-article bill under discussion in the House of Representatives would provide specific penalties for deepfake abuses and digital manipulation.

Al3omk reports the minister delegate for digital transition, Amal El Fallah Seghrouchni, telling parliament in a written answer that the ministry is preparing a digital administration bill with AI-specific provisions that takes account of personal data protection and information security.

EuroMedAI says Organic Law No. 53.25, promulgated by Dahir No. 1.25.70 on 16 January 2026, names AI tools among the means of electoral offences, including a new Article 51 bis on fabricated content, with penalties of 2 to 5 years and MAD 50,000-100,000.

EuroMedAI says HACA Decision No. 50-26 of 16 June 2026 prohibits broadcasting falsified or AI-generated electoral content liable to mislead the public and requires a notice on AI-generated educational content on radio and television.

EuroMedAI says HACA, the audiovisual authority, adopted Decision No. 50-26 on AI-generated electoral content on radio and television, and the CNDP issued guidance in late August 2026 asking that AI-produced content be identified.

Le360 reports that the Moroccan digital-transition department has prepared a draft digitalisation bill that will frame AI in administrative processes, covering algorithm transparency, the right to explanation and to contest automated decisions, and non-discrimination.
The CNDP stated that AI processing of personal data is governed by Law 09-08, and that automatic decisions need attention so citizens keep access to redress.
The CNDP stated that one of its missions is to ensure that AI processing of personal data complies with Law 09-08.
